t.5.62.1: Thus addressed by Sugrīva, the monkey Dadhimukha, delighted, respectfully saluted Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva.
t.5.62.3: Just as he had come before, so he went back in haste; descending from the sky to the earth, he entered that forest.
t.5.62.2: Having bowed to Sugrīva and to the two mighty Rāghavas, he leapt up into the sky together with the valiant monkeys.
t.5.62.4: Having entered the Madhuvana, he saw all the monkey chiefs, intoxicated and unruly, passing honey-water as urine.
t.5.62.5: That hero approached them and, joining his hands together in reverent salutation, joyfully spoke these gentle words to Aṅgada.
t.5.62.6: O gentle one, you should not be angry that you were held back by these guards; it was out of ignorance and anger that the guards stopped you all.
t.5.62.7: You are the crown prince and the lord of this forest, O mighty one. The offence that was committed earlier out of foolishness, your honour ought to forgive.
t.5.62.8: For just as your father was formerly the lord of the monkey hosts, so too are you, and Sugrīva, and no one else, O best of monkeys.
t.5.62.10: Hearing of your arrival together with these leaders of the monkey troops, he was overjoyed; and though he heard that the grove had been ravaged, he was not angry.
t.5.62.9: For I went and reported to your paternal uncle, O sinless one, the arrival here of all these forest-dwellers.
t.5.62.11: Your paternal uncle Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, was overjoyed, and the king said to me, “Send them all quickly.”
t.5.62.12: Having heard these gentle words of Dadhimukha, Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, skilled in speech, spoke these words to them.
t.5.62.13: I suspect, O leaders of the monkey troops, that this news has already been heard by Rāma. Therefore, O scorchers of foes, it is not fitting for us to remain here now that the task has been accomplished.
t.5.62.14: The forest-dwellers have drunk honey as much as they pleased and are now rested. What remains but to go there, where Sugrīva, my elder, is?
t.5.62.15: Whatever all the leaders of the monkey troops tell me when they have assembled, that I shall do in this matter that must be done, for I am subject to you.
t.5.62.16: Even though I am the crown prince, I am not in a position to command you. It is not proper for me to assail you, who have accomplished your task.
t.5.62.17: Hearing the unfailing words of Aṅgada as he spoke thus, the forest-dwellers, their minds filled with delight, spoke these words.
t.5.62.18: O king, bull among monkeys, who that is a lord would speak like this? For everyone intoxicated with the pride of power thinks only, 'It is I.'
t.5.62.19: These words are truly worthy of you and of no one else, for your humility proclaims the auspicious good fortune that is yet to be yours.
t.5.62.20: All of us too have arrived, resolved to go there where Sugrīva, the imperishable lord of the monkey heroes, is.
t.5.62.21: For without being told by you, O best of monkeys, the monkeys cannot go anywhere even a single step; this truth we tell you.
t.5.62.22: While they were speaking thus, Aṅgada replied, and having said, "Very well, let us go," he leapt up from the surface of the earth.
t.5.62.23: As he leapt up, all those leaders of the monkey troops leapt up after him, making the sky skyless, like fires flung up from a sacrifice.
t.5.62.25: Even before Aṅgada had arrived, Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, spoke to the lotus-eyed Rāma, who was stricken with grief.
t.5.62.24: Those swift monkeys suddenly leapt up into the sky, roaring a mighty roar, like clouds driven by the wind.
t.5.62.26: Take heart, may good fortune be yours; the queen has been found, there is no doubt. For once the time set by us had passed, they could not have come here otherwise.
t.5.62.27: For had the task been brought to ruin, the crown prince Aṅgada, mighty-armed and foremost among the leaping monkeys, would not come into my presence.
t.5.62.28: Even if such an undertaking could occur among those who had not accomplished their task, he would then surely be downcast of face, his mind bewildered and agitated.
t.5.62.29: This Madhuvana of mine, inherited from father and grandfather and guarded by our forebears, the lord of the monkeys would never ravage unless he were filled with joy.
t.5.62.30: Kausalyā is blessed with a noble son, O Rāma; take heart, O you of steadfast vows! The queen has been found, there is no doubt, and by none other than Hanumān, for no one else of such a kind could be the means of accomplishing this task.
t.5.62.31: For in Hanumān, O best among the wise, there are surely success and wisdom, resolve and valour, just as brilliance abides ever in the sun.
t.5.62.32: Where Jāmbavān is the leader, Aṅgada the lord of the army, and Hanumān too the one in command, the outcome of that venture cannot be otherwise.
t.5.62.33: Do not now be filled with anxiety, O you of immeasurable valour.
t.5.62.34: Then he heard, close at hand in the sky, the joyous cries of "kilakilā" from the forest-dwellers as they roared, elated by Hanūmān's deed, having come to Kiṣkindhā as though proclaiming their success.
t.5.62.35: Then, hearing that clamour of the monkeys, the best of monkeys, his tail stretched out and curled, became glad at heart.
t.5.62.36: Those monkeys, too, came, longing to see Rāma, placing Aṅgada and the monkey Hanūmān at their head.
t.5.62.37: Those heroes, led by Aṅgada, thrilled and filled with joy, alighted near the king of the monkeys and near Rāghava.
t.5.62.38: Then the mighty Hanumān, bowing his head, reported to Rāghava that the queen was steadfast in her vows and unharmed.
t.5.62.39: Then Lakṣmaṇa, filled with joy, looked with great respect upon the delighted Sugrīva, whose mind was firmly settled about the matter concerning the son of the Wind.
t.5.62.40: Then Rāghava, slayer of enemy heroes, rejoicing with delight, looked upon Hanūmān with great esteem.
